subject: ClearWave — inference cost pressure: summary + ops asks
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@clearwave.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: ClearWave — inference cost pressure: summary + ops asks

Hi Ellen — thanks for taking the time today. Quick write-up of what we heard, success criteria you articulated, and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

TL;DR: main pain is runaway token unit cost + peak concurrency causing tail-latency spikes. You’re open to aggressive batching/caching and selective quantization if accuracy tests look good. Next step: send sample traffic & prompt set; schedule technical deep dive with SE (Aditya) to agree pilot matrix.

What we heard (pain points)
- Unit economics: token spend grew ~3x in the last 6 months after product changes; finance has a hard cap for Q3.
- Tail latency during concurrent inference peaks (checkout flows) — blocking conversions.
- Current model variants: fine-tuned Llama-derived models served on GCP VMs (mixed GPUs), limited autoscaling due to cold-starts.
- Instrumentation gap: limited token-level billing and incomplete KV/prefix cache visibility.

Success criteria you called out
- Reduce per-token cost by 30–50% without >2% drop in intent/QA metrics.
- P95 latency at peak traffic <= 300ms for short-form prompts (<= 128 tokens).
- Clear measurement: per-route cost and accuracy baseline to evaluate regressions.

Suggested pilot (high-level)
1) Data: you provide representative prompt set + 48h token-level traffic trace (sample).
2) Pilot window: 2 weeks with staged variants (hosted + quantized variants) on a mirrored workload.
3) Metrics: token unit cost, p50/p95 latency, accuracy delta on provided eval set.
4) Ops: Redwood provides batching/caching config recommendations, quantization profiles to test.

Immediate asks / next steps (owners & dates)
- Ellen / ClearWave: upload token-profile + sample prompts to Drive link by Thu 5/21. (Attachments referenced below)
- Logan (me): coordinate SE deep-dive (propose week of 5/24), share pilot template.
- Aditya (cc): run a brief feasibility check on quantization risk for your fine-tuned weights once we have the sample prompts.

Attachments: call-recording.mp3 (audio), initial_suggested_pilot_template.xlsx (pilot template) — I’ll drop both to the Drive folder.

Proposed meeting slots for SE deep-dive: Tue 5/25 10:00–11:00 PT, Wed 5/26 14:00–15:00 PT. Please confirm preferred slot and I’ll send calendar invite.

Thanks again — feel free to reply with any corrections to the notes.

Best,
Logan Wright
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

- We have a lightweight prefix cache implemented in-app but it’s not durable across instances (so misses on scale-outs).
- We care a lot about accuracy — some prompts are user-SL sensitive, so any quantization needs to be audited against our evaluation suite.

What we will share
- I’m attaching a 24h token profile export (clearwave_token_profile.csv) and a small prompt sample set.
- Procurement looped in to start surfacing any SOW / NDA questions early — procurement@clearwave.ai.

- What accuracy delta should we expect from int8 / int4 quantization on similar Llama-2-derived models?
- Do you have a suggested baseline config for batching that will avoid increasing p95 latency for short prompts?
- High-level pricing: we want hosted pricing vs a small dedicated pool estimate so procurement can model costs.

We’ll aim to get the sample data into the Drive folder by Thu 5/21. Confirmed — 5/25 10:00 PT works for the team for the technical deep-dive.

Redwood checklist for deep-dive (please upload to Drive before the call)

- Representative prompt set + expected output length per route (csv).

- A small eval set with pass/fail labels we can use for quick accuracy comparisons.

Pilot kickoff plan (short)

- Week 1: run baseline, collect metrics.
- Week 2: apply batching + caching tweaks, test quantized variants (int8 first), measure accuracy delta.

- We’ll produce a quick hosted vs small-dedicated estimate after the deep-dive once we see the token profile & peak concurrency. For procurement: our Hosted model charges per-token with volume tiers; Dedicated includes committed throughput pricing and lower per-token compute. We’ll include a sample cost model in the pilot template.

Hi Ellen / Logan — looping in a short pilot design I’ll present Tuesday and a couple upfront notes:

Pilot design (summary)
- Variants: baseline (current float32), int8 quantized, aggressive batching + prefix cache enabled, and a small dedicated pool mirror.
- Evaluation matrix: token-unit-cost, p50/p95 latency, top-1 accuracy on eval set, and memory footprint.
- Risk controls: A/B gating on accuracy with rollback thresholds (default 2% metric delta).

Quick notes on quantization expectations
- Int8: typical compute reduction 2–3x vs float32 with small accuracy deltas on many Llama-derived models; correctness depends on calibration data and per-layer quant configs.
- Int4: higher risk for our fine-tuned variants — we’ll only suggest int4 in the later stage after validating int8.

I’ve uploaded pilot_matrix.xlsx and model_variant_q_profiles.pdf to the Drive folder. I’ll prepare a short checklist to run in a small mirror during Week 1.

See you Tue 10:00 PT.
